{{Short description|Mathematical result about equivariant K-theory in homotopy theory}}
The '''Atiyah–Segal completion theorem''' is a [[theorem]] in [[mathematics]] about [[equivariant]] [[K-theory]] in [[homotopy theory]]. Let ''G'' be a [[compact group|compact]] [[Lie group]] and let ''X'' be a ''G''-[[CW-complex]]. The theorem then states that the projection map

:<math>\pi\colon X\times EG\to X</math>

induces an isomorphism of [[profinite group|prorings]]

:<math>\pi^*\colon K_G^*(X)_{\widehat{I\,}} \to K^*((X\times EG)/G).</math>

Here, the induced map has as [[Domain of a function|domain]] the [[completion (ring theory)|completion]] of the ''G''-equivariant K-theory of ''X'' with respect to ''I'', where ''I'' denotes the [[augmentation ideal]] of the [[representation ring]] of ''G''.

In the special case of ''X'' being a point, the theorem specializes to give an isomorphism <math>K^*(BG)\cong R(G)_{\widehat{I\,}}</math> between the K-theory of the [[classifying space]] of ''G'' and the completion of the representation ring.

The theorem can be interpreted as giving a comparison between the geometrical process of taking the homotopy quotient of a ''G''-space, by making the [[Group action (mathematics)|action]] free before passing to the quotient, and the algebraic process of completing with respect to an ideal.<ref name=Greenlees>{{cite conference
 | author = Greenlees, J.P.C.
 | year = 1996
 | title = An introduction to equivariant K-theory.
 | conference = Equivariant homotopy and cohomology theory
 | book-title = CBMS Regional Conference Series
 | volume = 91
 | pages = 143–152
 | publisher = Published for the Conference Board of the Mathematical Sciences, Washington, DC
}}</ref>

The theorem was first proved for [[finite groups]] by [[Michael Atiyah]] in 1961,<ref name=Atiyah1961>{{cite journal
 | last = Atiyah|first= M.F.|author-link=Michael Atiyah
 | year = 1961
 | title = Characters and cohomology of finite groups
 |journal= Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS| volume = 9
 | issue = 1
 | pages = 23–64
 |doi= 10.1007/BF02698718|s2cid= 54764252|url= http://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1961__9__23_0/}}</ref>
and a proof of the general case was published by Atiyah together with [[Graeme Segal]] in 1969.<ref name=Atiyah1969>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Atiyah|first1= M.F.|author1-link=Michael Atiyah
 | last2 = Segal|first2= G.B.|author2-link=Graeme Segal
 | year = 1969
 | title = Equivariant K-theory and completion
 | journal = [[Journal of Differential Geometry]]
 | volume = 3
 |issue= 1–2| pages = 1–18
 | url = http://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~aar/papers/atiyahsegal1.pdf
 | accessdate = 2008-06-19
|doi= 10.4310/jdg/1214428815| doi-access = free
 }}</ref>
Different proofs have since appeared generalizing the theorem to completion with respect to families of subgroups.<ref name=Jackowski1985>{{cite journal
 | last = Jackowski | first= S.
 | year = 1985
 | title = Families of subgroups and completion
 | journal = J. Pure Appl. Algebra
 | volume = 37
 | issue = 2
 | pages = 167–179
 | doi = 10.1016/0022-4049(85)90094-5
| doi-access = free
 }}</ref><ref name=Adams1988>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Adams | first1= J.F.
 | last2 = Haeberly|first2= J.P.|last3= Jackowski|first3= S. |last4=May|first4= J.P.|author4-link=J. Peter May
 | year = 1988
 | title = A generalization of the Atiyah-Segal Completion Theorem
 | journal = Topology
 | volume = 27
 | issue = 1
 | pages = 1–6
 | doi = 10.1016/0040-9383(88)90002-X
| doi-access = free}}</ref>
The corresponding statement for algebraic K-theory was proven by [[Alexander Merkurjev]], holding in the case that the group is algebraic over the complex numbers.
